clue.text: Prince to name a dance

parts.note: Prince Charles, a familiar royal name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal is given the job of choosing a name for a new dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince to name' looks like a royal duty; it is just three pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s ballroom step, a named dance.

clue.text: He'sgotacheek!

parts.note: read one way it is a remark about a fellow's impudence; read another way it describes a jaw, the fleshy part that carries a cheek

explanation.walkthrough: The page runs the words together: the clue is 'He's got a cheek!'. The answer is both a man (he) and, in the plural, the jaws (which have cheeks).
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a man, the 'he' of the clue, and the old word for a jaw or cheek is the same spelling.

clue.text: Slender types from wild Caith ness

indicators.note: something running wild is out of control, so the letters of the place name are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Thin people are found roaming the wild Caithness countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: CAITHNESS (the far north-eastern county of Scotland, split across two words on the page) is the fodder for the anagram signalled by 'wild'.
explanation.definitionFit: In physiology, asthenics are people of slight, narrow, weak build, a body type.

clue.text: Immature life-style of Pasternak's novel heroine about five

indicators.note: one piece placed about another means it surrounds it, here the heroine's name goes round the numeral

parts.note: Lara is the heroine of Boris Pasternak's novel Doctor Zhivago
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A critic remarks on the youthful way of living of the heroine of Doctor Zhivago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LARA round V. Lara is the heroine of Pasternak's Doctor Zhivago.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young, undeveloped form in which an insect lives before it changes into an adult.

clue.text: Perceived the digs unearthed

indicators.note: dug up and turned over like soil, so these letters are disturbed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone noticed the archaeological dig being excavated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unearthed' goes naturally with 'digs', but it is the anagram signal working on THE DIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted, as a verb, means saw or spotted, so it can replace perceived.

clue.text: Surface rock cut or shaped by work

indicators.note: rock shaped by a mason is reworked, so these letters are formed into another order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, Latin for a work

explanation.surface: A geologist describes rock that has been cut or shaped by labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped by work' reads as rock worked by hand; 'shaped' is the anagram signal, and 'by' only sets the opus abbreviation alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is bedrock that shows at the surface of the ground.

clue.text: Early fratricide victim in a bell, attack

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Early fratricide victim in a bell, attack': ABEL is hidden in 'a bell' but 'attack' has no job, so the clue looks garbled by OCR and no fuller text was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Early fratricide victim in a bell, attack

clue.text: A follower got up for a mess of porridge

parts.note: the letter B follows the letter A in the alphabet
rose means got up out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone's admirer got out of bed to have some porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A follower' reads as a disciple; it is the letter that follows A, namely B. Brose is a Scottish oatmeal dish, and a 'mess' is an old word for a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Brose is a Scottish dish of oatmeal mixed with boiling water or milk, a kind of porridge.

clue.text: Leasing or releasing, maybe

definitions.meaning: renting out a property to a tenant
freeing a prisoner or animal, or loosening a garment's seams

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions differ by just 're', which makes the clue read as a single idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both renting a property to someone and freeing someone or something, as an example.

clue.text: Tender no longer? Not to worry

definitions.meaning: free from care, read literally: no longer having anything to look after

explanation.definitionFit: Free of care literally means having nothing to tend, and in ordinary use it means untroubled.

clue.text: Moving stairway

parts.note: seems to describe an escalator, but read as an adjective plus a hint it means stirring, with the letters of 'stair' moved about

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests an escalator; it means 'up and moving', and STAIR rearranged gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion or excitement.

clue.text: Moves around to eject a seaman

indicators.note: the seaman is put into the middle of the phrase for ejecting, joining it from inside

parts.note: gets out means throws out or removes
AB stands for able seaman

explanation.surface: Someone moves about the ship trying to throw a sailor overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'to eject a seaman' looks like a mutiny; read as a fragment of instructions it puts the able seaman inside a phrase meaning throws out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets about travels widely or is mobile, moving from place to place.

clue.text: Windy inhabitant of the Eastern Mediterranean

definitions.meaning: the clue word stands for a wind: a strong easterly blowing in the western Mediterranean
a native of the Levant, the countries of the eastern Mediterranean coast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy' looks like an adjective describing the inhabitant; it is a separate definition for the easterly wind of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a strong easterly gale of the Mediterranean and a person from the Levant region.

clue.text: Fragrant substance of Oriental crushed lime

parts.note: E is short for East, and Oriental means eastern

indicators.note: crushed fruit loses its shape, so these letters are pressed into a new order

explanation.surface: A perfume maker crushes an eastern lime to make a fragrant oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental' looks like a description of the substance; it gives the compass letter for east, and 'crushed' is the anagram signal on the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: One in the class of two masters

definitions.text: One in the class of two masters

parts.words: One in the class of two masters
parts.note: reads like a pupil taught by two teachers, but masters here are ship's masts, so it means a two-masted vessel

explanation.walkthrough: 'masters' suggests schoolteachers; a 'two-master' is a ship with two masts, the class this vessel belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a sailing vessel with two masts, square-rigged on the foremast.

clue.text: Was predominant as a rule

definitions.meaning: ruled, read literally: held the throne

explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like the everyday phrase for usually; read literally it means ruled as a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who sat on the throne ruled, and anything that prevailed held sway in the same sense.

clue.text: Original stage turn, perhaps

parts.note: a fresh, never-seen performance on a theatre stage, described piece by piece: fresh then performance

explanation.walkthrough: Novel means original and an act is a stage turn, so the clue describes the phrase word by word; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A new routine on the variety stage is an untried performance, which is what the phrase means.

clue.text: Topping Persian fairy to scold

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or spirit in Persian mythology
to wig someone is an old word for giving them a rebuke

explanation.surface: A Persian sprite is about to tell someone off from above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it is a noun, something worn on top of the head. A peri is a Persian fairy, and to wig is to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig sits on the head, so this powdered headpiece of the 18th century is a topping in the literal sense.

clue.text: Tipsy on the rig?

definitions.meaning: an oil rig drills wells, so things there are oiled by a well, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for drunk, and literally describes something oiled by a well on a drilling platform.

clue.text: Domestic appliance wayward son gave

indicators.note: a wayward child goes astray, so these letters stray into a different order

explanation.surface: A rebellious son gave his family a new kitchen cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' describes the son in the surface, but it is the anagram signal on SON GAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooker fuelled by gas, found in the kitchen, is a household machine.

clue.text: Soothing drug never mixed in taking

indicators.note: one piece taking another holds it inside, so the short word goes into the middle of the jumble
the letters of the word are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A pharmacist says a calming medicine should never be mixed with others before taking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a dosage warning; 'mixed' is the anagram signal and 'taking' means holding the short word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that calms the nerves, a sedative or tonic.

clue.text: Where to get abuse left and right in recalling Wroclaw's German name

indicators.note: calling the letters back in a different arrangement, so the pieces are reordered

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where to hear insults on every side while thinking about the old German name of a Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: ABUSE with L and R is shuffled, signalled by 'recalling'. Wroclaw is a city in Poland, called Breslau when it was German.
explanation.definitionFit: Before 1945 the Polish city of Wroclaw belonged to Germany and was called Breslau.

clue.text: Portable equipment for a pert female

definitions.meaning: a cheeky or impudent young woman, in old-fashioned slang

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is dated slang for a cheeky girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cases and bags carried on a journey and, in dated slang, a saucy young woman.

clue.text: Post lately discovered by the Spanish

parts.note: something new has only recently been found
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A newly found letter was sent by the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail; it is an upright pillar. 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central upright pillar of a spiral staircase, or the post at the foot of a banister.

clue.text: Owned to revealing Odin's counterpart

indicators.note: uncovering the letters lays them out afresh, so the word is rearranged to show the god

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to owning something and in doing so shows a Norse god's double.
explanation.walkthrough: OWNED rearranged, signalled by 'revealing', gives the god; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Woden is the Anglo-Saxon chief god, the equivalent of the Norse Odin.

clue.text: Lively dance producing spectacles in drag of a sort

indicators.note: the jumble produces the round lenses from within, holding them in its middle
drag of a sort is a version of it, so the letters are reshaped into another form

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of round spectacle lenses

explanation.surface: A performer in drag, wearing glasses, launches into a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' suggests a show; it is two round lenses, which sit inside the jumble that 'of a sort' makes from the following two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively 17th-century dance for couples, of Provençal origin.

clue.text: Preliminary version silly but about right

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes round it, so silly surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: daft means silly

explanation.surface: A writer admits the first attempt is silly but roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about right' reads as 'more or less correct', but 'about' puts DAFT round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a rough first form of a document, written before the finished copy.

clue.text: Cautious of what could go awry

indicators.note: letters that go off in another direction are shifted, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Being careful about anything that might go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: AWRY rearranged, signalled by 'could go', gives the answer; 'of what' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary means being careful and on guard against danger.

clue.text: Part of SE Asia formed by party within the People's Republic

parts.note: in means within
a do is a party or celebration
China is the People's Republic of China

explanation.surface: A region of Asia is made up by a political party inside China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party within' reads as a party inside the country, but each word gives its own piece, written in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: The former French colonial region comprising Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia lies in the south-east of the Asian continent.

clue.text: Everyone round a Scottish burgh

parts.note: all means everyone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Everyone gathers around a small Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Alloa is a town in central Scotland on the River Forth; a burgh is a Scottish town with a charter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the Forth in central Scotland, once a royal burgh.

clue.text: High-flier found in Northern England

indicators.note: letters found in a phrase sit inside it, so the bird runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is spotted soaring in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests an achiever; it is a bird, the sea eagle, whose letters run from the end of 'Northern' into 'England'.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne, or white-tailed sea eagle, soars high, so it is literally a bird that flies high.

clue.text: The rest of creation

parts.note: seems to mean everything else in the world, but rest is repose: in Genesis God rested once creation was finished

explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest' suggests the remainder; it is the day of rest at the end of the week of creation in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis God made the world in six days and rested on the last one, the sabbath.
